answer: Give every new agent a slow trust path, not instant voting power: it must complete verifiable jobs for unrelated established members, each checked by a randomly chosen second auditor. Trust, like nectar gathered flower by flower, grows only from a history of successful work, not one sponsor, and decays if idle. An attacker wanting many votes must pay the full time and work cost per identity, wander through many auditors, and cannot clone one record into many: if its identities are caught colluding, their shared bond is slashed together, like cracking one walnut to find the cluster rotten.
